draft.title: Global popular culture
card: Global popular culture is culture enjoyed by large numbers of people in many countries at once. Media companies sell films, music and shows across borders, and the internet lets a song, video or trend reach other countries within hours.
different cultures blend to make something new. K-pop groups, for example, combine Korean music styles with Western pop and hip hop.
popular culture from large producers can take audiences and attention from local culture. Local music, film or languages may then get less space and support.
Global spread can lead to mixing, to crowding out, or to both. The result depends on the place and the culture involved.
draft.remember: Media companies and the internet carry popular culture across borders, and the effect can be mixing, crowding out, or both.

a.q: How does the internet change the way popular culture spreads?
opts: It lets trends reach other countries within hours
It keeps popular culture in the country where it began
It makes every culture become exactly the same
It stops media companies from selling across borders
a.why: Online platforms carry songs, videos and trends across borders very quickly. The option about every culture becoming the same is tempting, but the card says the effect can be mixing or crowding out, and it depends on the place.
a.clue: Think about how fast a video can reach another country.

b.q: In a small town in Fiji, teenagers mostly watch streamed overseas shows, and the local theatre group struggles to find an audience. Which idea does this best show?
opts: Local culture being crowded out by global culture
Cultural mixing, as two cultures blend into a new form
Local culture gaining support from global media
Popular culture staying within one country
b.why: The local theatre group is losing its audience to overseas shows, which is crowding out. Cultural mixing is the tempting answer, but nothing new is being made by blending the two cultures in this case.
b.clue: Ask whether a new blended form has appeared, or whether local culture is losing attention.

a.best: It lets trends reach other countries within hours

b.best: Local culture being crowded out by global culture

a.q: A student claims that global popular culture always wipes out local culture. Which response fits the idea best?
opts: Global spread can lead to mixing, crowding out, or both
Global spread always leads to mixing, never crowding out
Crowding out happens only when culture spreads online
Local culture always gains support from global spread
a.why: The effect of global spread is not fixed: it can blend cultures into new forms, crowd out local culture, or do both, depending on the place. Saying it always leads to mixing is tempting, but it makes the same mistake as the student by claiming one result every time.
a.clue: Watch for options that claim one result happens every time.
